Okay, quick and dirty politics lesson. Here's some of the basics of what Fascism is:

  • Ultra-nationalism. The highest priority is not peace, not economic performance, but the well-being of your nation.

  • Tendency toward "racism", or generally ethnostatism. The belief is that your nation is not simply anyone living in some borders paying taxes to the same government. Your nation is the people who share a heritage, a history, a culture, a community with you. The idea that that these people have the right to live among and rule themselves without outside interference, or the need to pretend that they are the same as anyone else.

  • Dictatorialism. The idea that the nation should be led by an authority that is not designed to be susceptible to outside pressure, and can rule (if they rule well) in the interests of the nation without owing their power to anyone else.

  • Private ownership without free markets. Again, the highest priority is the good of the nation. Private business and private ownership is allowed, but the authority will tightly regulate anything that they think is a risk to the people, regardless of profit. You can buy and sell at whatever prices the market decides, and you genuinely own whatever you buy, in nearly all cases. But you will see heavy regulation of industry if it is thought that you are degenerating the culture or destroying the land or are a threat to the people's health, etc.

  • Tendency to focus on hierarchy and the promotion of health and strength, rather than equality and the honoring of victimhood. This is one of the areas where they most become very anti-liberal and anti-Marxist.

  • Tendency toward militarism. The thought that a strong military is necessary for a stable nation, and that there is nothing wrong with fighting to secure and benefit your people.
